title: CSV Coordinate Centroid Calculator
description: Find the mean latitude and longitude of a coordinate CSV with the CSV Coordinate Centroid Calculator — the file's balance point, honestly simple. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, five US cities (New York, Chicago, Los Angeles, Houston, Denver) balance at 37.2285, −96.0479 — in Kansas, south of Wichita, where no city on the list actually is.
quick_answer: The CSV Coordinate Centroid Calculator finds the simple arithmetic mean latitude and longitude of a coordinate list — the file’s balance point. Paste the CSV and read the centre: a first map centre and an honest mean — not population-weighted, not a polygon’s mass centroid.

This quarter’s mean versus last quarter’s shows drift — a sales territory creeping west announces itself in the centroid before any report.
A mean point is a starting guess for central facilities — refine it with road-network tools afterwards, but start from the data’s balance, not a hunch.

Five cities average to 37.2285, −96.0479. Los Angeles pulls west, Houston pulls south, and the mean lands where means land — the balance point is a statistic, not a destination, and Kansas is used to hosting them.

popular_table.note: The arithmetic mean treats latitude and longitude as flat numbers — right for local and national files. Planet-spanning sets and date-line crossers belong to spherical averaging (the Coordinate Mean Calculator).

faq: Is the centroid a real place in my data?
Usually not — it is the balance point of all rows, which may sit in a lake or a neighbouring state. It summarises the file; it is not one of the file’s points.
This calculator is the plain mean — every row counts once. Weighted centres need the weight column honoured, which is a deliberate step up in tooling.
Duplicates vote twice. Deduplicate first if repeats are accidents; keep them if repeats are frequency (deliveries per address is a weight in disguise).
Unparseable rows cannot join the average. Validate the file first so the centre is computed from the data you meant.
Latitude averaged flat — is that wrong?
For files within a country it is the standard exploratory statistic. The distortion grows near poles and across the date line; the spherical mean is the upgrade path, linked from this page.
The mean of the stop list — a fair summary of where the route lives, though the route’s operational centre is a road question.
Can I centre a map on it?
That is its day job: paste the pair into any map or the Latitude Longitude Finder and the view opens on your data’s balance.
